title: What IF You Could Walk Through Walls?
format: Long-form 20m43s 16:9 (854x480 @30fps download), second-person ('you') narrated superpower story with ~25 short voiced character lines, low-poly 3D toon animation. Category People & Blogs. Description repeats the premise + three teaser problems ('the floor is a wall too, your phone stays behind, and you can never stop halfway') and links a sister episode (Turn Invisible). Ends 'TO BE CONTINUED' with a 'Project IF' series hook.

title_pattern.template: What IF You Could [Superpower Verb Phrase]?
title_pattern.type: channel-branded hypothetical question (capital IF = brand IFOLOGY), 2nd-person power fantasy
title_pattern.notes: Identical template to the channel's outliers (Stop Time 6.15x, 10x Faster 8.38x, Shapeshift 4.21x), so the title alone does not explain the gap. 'Walk through walls' is a familiar, lower-stakes power (phasing) than time-stop/speed, and the title promises no danger or twist; the thumbnail text 'LOCKED? SO WHAT.' frames it as a heist/convenience power rather than a risk. The runtime (20.7 min, ~2x the outliers) also likely hurt.
variants_to_try: What IF You Could Walk Through Walls... But Couldn't Stop Halfway?
What IF You Got Stuck Inside a Wall?
You Can Walk Through Walls. The Floor Is a Wall Too.

thumbnail.composition: Rule-of-thirds split: left 45% = deep purple bank-lobby corridor (pillars, wall sconces, CCTV camera with red light top-left, bank-pillar logo banner), right 40% = huge steel vault door filling the edge; the stickman protagonist bursts out of the vault door at centre-right, half his body emerging through the metal with cyan ripple rings at the contact line. Text block bottom-left over the corridor.
thumbnail.text: 'LOCKED?' (white, heavy condensed sans, black outline) over 'SO WHAT.' (yellow, same font, black outline) - two lines, ~5 words total.
thumbnail.colours: Purple/violet ambient with warm amber sconce highlights; cool gunmetal vault; the subject is the saturation peak: royal-blue hoodie, glossy gold bar, cyan phasing glow; white+yellow text. Strong warm/cool split.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Character head+torso ~45% of frame height, much larger than in-video framing; the black sphere head with a mischievous grin (angled eyebrows, wide smile) is the darkest, most contrasty shape. The gold bar held up at chest height is a second focal point. Scale contrast = big character vs. huge vault vs. tiny CCTV camera (implied 'they can't stop me').
thumbnail.why_it_works: Shows the power in action (body half inside solid steel) plus a forbidden payoff (stolen gold bar) and a smug attitude - wish-fulfilment + mild transgression. Text is a cocky answer rather than a question. Weakness vs the channel's outliers: it promises a heist that the video never delivers (the story is a wholesome kid-next-door rescue), and there is no danger/curiosity element (no 'what went wrong'), so it reads as a fun power, not a high-stakes one.
thumbnail.style_note: Thumbnail is a more detailed, painterly 2D-illustration render (outlined character, glossy materials) than the in-video low-poly 3D - upgraded art for the thumb.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: "You're 9-years-old and you're locked in the upstairs bathroom. Not on purpose, the old lock on the door is stuck."
hook.verbatim_0_67s_summary: Locked-in-bathroom kid; dad goes for a screwdriver; kid leans his forehead on the door and 'the door goes soft, like cold jelly that isn't wet'; 1 s of total black ('You can't see. You can't hear. It smells like nothing at all'); falls out flat on the hallway carpet; door still locked, no hole. Dad returns: 'How did you get out?' / 'I used the door.' / 'The door is locked.' / 'Not for me, I guess.' -> 'So, what if you could walk through walls? Not break them, not climb over them, walk straight through them, like they were made of fog. Here's how it works.'
hook.visual_0_5s: Over-the-shoulder of a small kid (black sphere head, grey hoodie) twisting a brass door knob in a white-tiled bathroom; 0:06 cut to the hallway side - dad (red striped shirt) jiggling the handle.
hook.device: In-medias-res 2nd-person cold open (age + trapped situation in the first sentence), accidental discovery of the power in a mundane setting, sensory description of the power (jelly/black/no smell), comedic deadpan dialogue button, then the title question restated with negation ('Not break them, not climb over them...') and a 'Here's how it works' promise. Title card 'WHAT IF YOU COULD WALK THROUGH WALLS?' at 1:08.
hook.notes: Same cold-open shape as the channel's outliers (scene -> discovery -> joke -> title question) but slower: 67 s before the title question vs. ~20-30 s in Stop Time / 10x Faster, and the next 3.5 min are pure science exposition (atoms, Rutherford, Pauli, tunneling) before the story resumes.

beats.summary: 2nd-person setup: you're 9, locked in the bathroom by a stuck lock; dad leaves for a screwdriver; you lean on the door.
Door goes soft like cold jelly; face sinks in; 1 s of total black and silence; fall out onto the hallway carpet; door intact, still locked.
Dad returns with screwdriver and flashlight, stares; deadpan exchange ending 'Not for me, I guess.'
'So, what if you could walk through walls?' restated by negation (not break, not climb), 'like fog'. 'Here's how it works.' Title card.
Atom count of a body (7 billion billion billion); Rutherford/Geiger/Marsden gold foil 1911, cannonball-at-tissue-paper quote; nucleus 100,000x smaller; stadium/pea analogy.

beats.beat_type: science 2: why we can't (rules of the world)
beats.summary: Question pivot 'why can't anybody walk through a wall? Two reasons': electron repulsion (magnets analogy) and the Pauli exclusion principle (1925, Nobel 1945); 'you're hovering on your chair' mind-blow fact.

Quantum tunneling; protons tunnel to fuse in the sun; 2025 Nobel (Clarke, Devoret, Martinis) for tunneling in a hand-sized circuit; 'once in a while a ball would end up on the other side'; odds for a whole person ~0 -> 'Except to you.'

That night: hand sinks into bedroom wall up to the elbow ('like sticking your arm into a cloud'); head pops out in little sister's room; sister screams 'There's a head in my wall!'; mom: 'You were dreaming.'

A month locked in your room: Rule 1 it's like holding a feeling (let go = solid); Rule 2 you can choose which part goes through (months of practice); Rule 3 inside a wall you're blind and deaf - getting lost in the closet wall for a minute -> your own rule 'always walk straight, never turn around inside anything' (planted for the climax).

Never knock, never need a key: pop the locked car, pull the cereal prize from the bottom, fetch the soccer ball through the fence, reach into the locker (Feastables bar), win tag, nobody plays hot potato with you; pranks - flipping cousin's cards through the table ('Nobody ever suspects the table'), head in the school wall next to the trophy case: Theo 'Why is your head in the wall?' 'I'm a trophy.'; talent show magic act, 2nd place to a juggler.
Face through the floor into the kitchen ceiling watching dad sing badly; walking slowly through an old tree and hearing sap 'like a river'; snow falling through your hand 'tickled by the sky'.

'A floor is just a wall that's lying down' + gravity; you sink through the bedroom floor onto the kitchen table in front of dad's cereal ('We have stairs.' 'I know.'); a summer learning to keep only the soles of your feet solid, 200 landings on the basement couch; never go through in the basement - dirt, rock, 'a very, very long way' (dread plant).

Power doesn't take clothes unless you concentrate: backpack stuck on the door, shoes left, hoodie with sleeves sticking out of the wood ('the door is waving at you'); phone stays inside the wall and rings at dinner; dad saws a hole and has 'stopped asking questions about you'; zipped pockets, lost socks.

No air inside a wall; house wall 4.5 in / 11 cm; brick and concrete thicker and unknown; breath-hold facts (most ~1 min; 2025 record 29 min 3 s by a Croatian freediver on pure oxygen) -> 'You're a kid with a power and a stopwatch'; safety line (never practise underwater or alone); Theo with the stopwatch: 'It's kind of purp-' 'I said, don't tell me.'

Banana test: finger inside, let go -> banana explodes (Pauli payoff), banana on the ceiling, fridge and sister; 'how much bigger a wall is than a banana'; 'You never let go inside anything again... Until the day you almost do.'

Late for class, halfway into the classroom wall when the principal says your name; wall starts hardening 'like cold jelly turning into cement'; you stumble out gasping minus one shoe; principal: 'Whose shoe is this?'; new rule: only for emergencies.

'Until the snowstorm': power out, neighbour Mr. Brennan (old, alone, full-size candy bars, waves every morning) - his dog never barks, now won't stop; faint 'Help! I fell!'; doors and windows locked; ambulance delayed by snow; mom on the phone; red brick wall of unknown thickness.

Biggest breath; hug your coat with your mind; lock your soles; step in. Total black, cold to the bones, counting steps 1...2...3, lost direction, recalls own rule 'walk straight, never turn around'; 4 -> fall into the laundry room onto towels.

Finds Mr. Brennan on the kitchen floor with the dog keeping him warm; blanket, pillow; unlocks the front door 'the normal way'; mom looks, doesn't ask; ambulance - he'll be okay; Brennan: 'There's no door in the laundry room... Next time, kid, you can just use the front door.'
Lying awake, hands smell like brick: you went into a wall you couldn't see through and somebody is going to be okay because of it.

'But there's one thing you didn't notice': an all-night laundromat across the street with lights on despite the power cut; a woman in a long grey coat watching the exact spot you entered; she leaves after the ambulance.
Next morning a small white card is half inside the wall above your bed - no slit, no hole: someone else can do what you do and was in your room last night. Card reads 'Project IF'.
'So, what would you do if you could walk through walls? Tell us in the comments, because this is only the beginning.' IFOLOGY logo, 'TO BE CONTINUED', subscribe lower-third.

pacing.scene_cut_method: ffmpeg select=gt(scene,0.3) on 480p (same as sibling IFOLOGY entries)
pacing.sampled_visual_change_s: ~3-4 (2 s samples change about every other frame; slow push-ins hold many shots)
pacing.re_hook_interval_s: Numbered structure gives a new chip/premise every ~60-80 s: Rule 1/2/3 (347-411), Problem 1-4 (553, 632, 709, 797), 'Until the day you almost do' (855), 'Until the snowstorm' (921), 'But there's one thing you didn't notice' (1147).
pacing.notes: Narration speed matches the outliers (~183-193 wpm) but the cut rate is roughly half (ASL 5.9 s vs 3.0-3.2 s on Stop Time / 10x Faster), the video is ~2x longer (20.7 min vs ~10 min), and 3.5 min of science exposition sits right after the hook (minutes 4-5 are the slowest cut rate: 6 and 4 cuts/min). Those are the clearest structural differences from the 4-8x outliers on the same channel.

art_style: Same IFOLOGY house style as its outliers: low-poly 3D toon shading, muted pastel suburban interiors, soft vignette and warm lamp light; characters with oversized matte-black sphere heads, cream rim light, chalk-like white eye/mouth decals, thin black limbs, colour-coded hoodies (protagonist grey -> teal/green later, Theo orange, sister navy, dad red stripes, mom yellow scarf, Mr. Brennan beige cardigan). Power signature = translucent frosted-glass body with white sparkle particles + concentric cyan/white ripple rings where the body meets a surface. Science segments switch to navy starfield 'micro world' with glowing atom spheres and a gridded floor. Text = small cream paper-label chips with dark serif caps, bottom-centre or top-left. Black vignette frames for 'inside the wall'.
techniques_worth_copying: Cold open in 2nd person with a concrete age + trapped situation in sentence one ('You're 9 and you're locked in the bathroom'), discovery of the power by accident, then a deadpan dialogue button before the title question.

Sensory description of the power (cold jelly that isn't wet, 1 s of black, smells like nothing) - makes an abstract power feel physical and gives the visuals a signature (translucency + ripple rings + black frame).

Real-science scaffolding with named people/years/numbers (Rutherford 1911, Pauli 1925/Nobel 1945, quantum tunneling, 2025 Nobel) and one relatable mind-blow ('you're hovering on your chair right now') - but keep it short.
Rules-of-the-power structure (Rule 1/2/3) then numbered Problems (1-4) as visible chips: built-in chaptering and a re-hook every ~60-80 s.

Plant-and-payoff discipline: 'never turn around inside anything' (6:47) is the thing that saves him in the climax (17:30); the banana/Pauli demo (13:43) sets the stakes for 'stopping halfway' in the near-miss (14:37); 'hug your clothes with your mind' and 'lock your soles' return in the climax checklist.
Concrete visual comedy per power use: hoodie sleeves waving from the door, phone ringing inside the wall, head as a trophy, banana on the sister - each gag is a single readable image.
Escalation ladder from fun -> inconvenience -> danger -> near-death -> heroic use: ends with a selfless rescue that recontextualises the power.
Counting device in total darkness (1...2...3...4 as big chips on black) - cheap to animate, very tense.
Sequel/universe hook: a mysterious watcher + an object half-embedded in the wall ('Project IF') + 'this is only the beginning' to feed the series and the comment CTA.
weaknesses_vs_outliers: Twice the runtime of the channel's 4-8x outliers (20.7 min vs ~10 min) with the same per-minute content density - a lot of middle montage.
3.5-min uninterrupted science block (1:16-4:27) right after the hook; slowest cut rate of the video (4-6 cuts/min) lands at minutes 4-5.
Thumbnail promises a bank heist (vault, gold bar, CCTV) that never happens; the actual story is a cosy kid-next-door rescue - promise/payoff mismatch.
Low danger in the title/thumbnail: the most clickable ideas (falling through the floor forever, getting stuck inside a wall, the banana explosion) are buried at 9-14 min instead of being the premise.
Cut rate roughly half the outliers (ASL 5.9 s vs ~3 s).
code_only_remake_needs: Character rig in SVG/Canvas: big black circle head with rim-light stroke, simple white eye/mouth decal set (neutral, wide-eyed, smug, scared, sleeping), thin limbs, hoodie torso in a colour token per character; pose library (stand, walk cycle, reach, lie flat, fall, sit, arm-raised 'idea').

Phasing effect: body opacity ~0.45 with white/frosted fill + additive sparkle particles; clip-path so the part 'inside' a wall is hidden and re-appears on the other side; concentric ripple-ring SVG circles (scale+fade) at the contact line.
'Inside the wall' scene: full black frame with radial vignette, subtle noise, big paper-chip numbers (1, 2, 3, 4) and a stopwatch readout.

2.5D sets as flat-shaded SVG rooms in perspective (bathroom tiles, hallway, bedrooms in teal/pink/lilac, kitchen, school hallway with lockers, classroom, snowy street, red-brick house, laundromat), warm lamp radial gradients and soft vignette; camera = slow push-in/pan via transform on a layered scene (parallax for depth).

Micro-world explainer kit: navy starfield with gridded floor, glowing atom spheres (radial gradients) with electron dots, repulsion animation, barrier + tunneling particle, proton fusion with + signs, stadium/pea scale shot, cross-section diagram (kitchen/basement/dirt/rock) with slow downward pan.
Historical reenactment template: candle-lit lab with chalkboard + stick scientists + 'YEAR - NAME' label chip.
Caption chip component: cream paper label, dark serif caps, slight drop shadow, pop-in scale; used for RULE n / PROBLEM n / quotes of dialogue / numbers (x200, 4.5 IN).
Particle systems: heavy diagonal snow, banana-mush splats, sparkle dust, music notes.

Narration: one TTS voice for the 2nd-person narrator at ~185 wpm plus 4-6 distinct voices for short character lines (dad, mom, sister, best friend, principal, old neighbour); music bed with stings on reveals; ringtone + dog bark SFX.
Outro kit: series card ('Project ...'), channel logo, 'TO BE CONTINUED' chip, subscribe lower-third.
Thumbnail kit: separate, more detailed illustration (outlined character, glossy prop, saturated hoodie, ripple glow at the wall line), two-line heavy sans text white over yellow with black stroke.
